text: Rafael Benítez Maudes, born on 16 April 1960, is a Spanish professional football manager and former player who is currently the head coach of Super League Greece club Panathinaikos. He joined Real Madrid's coaching staff at age 26, serving as under-19 and reserve team coach, and later as assistant manager for the senior team. He left Real Madrid in 1995, with brief and unsuccessful stints at Real Valladolid and Osasuna. He led Segunda División club Extremadura to promotion in the 1997–98 season, finishing second behind Alavés after winning 23 of 42 games, but the team was relegated in 1999 after finishing 17th and losing a play-off to Rayo Vallecano. He left Extremadura and coached Tenerife in 2000, winning promotion to La Liga by finishing third behind Sevilla and Real Betis. In 2001, Benítez was appointed coach of Valencia, replacing Héctor Cúper, and won La Liga in the 2001–02 and 2003–04 seasons, along with the UEFA Cup in the latter. After leaving Valencia, he joined English Premier League club Liverpool in June 2004, becoming the first Spaniard to manage in the league. He guided Liverpool to victory in the UEFA Champions League in 2005, reaching the final after a dramatic comeback in the "Miracle of Istanbul," and won the FA Cup in 2006. He also reached the 2007 Champions League final but failed to win the Premier League, with the best league finish under his management being second place in 2008–09. After leaving Liverpool in June 2010, he was appointed manager of Inter Milan, where he won the Supercoppa Italiana and Club World Cup but was dismissed midway through the 2010–11 season. In November 2012, he served as interim manager of Chelsea, winning the 2013 Europa League. He returned to Italy in 2013 to coach Napoli, where he won the Coppa Italia and Supercoppa Italiana. He then left Napoli and became coach of Real Madrid in June 2015 on a three-year contract, which lasted six months. Benítez was appointed manager of Newcastle United in March 2016, but was unable to avoid relegation; he earned promotion back to the Premier League by winning the Championship. He left in June 2019 and joined Chinese Super League club Dalian Professional, leaving by mutual consent in January 2021 before taking over at Everton in June. He was dismissed in January 2022 and managed Celta Vigo in 2023–24. As a player, Benítez played as a midfielder for Real Madrid Aficionados in the Tercera División and Real Madrid Castilla in the Segunda División, and earned a degree in physical education from INEF, the sports faculty at the Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, in 1982. In 1979, he played for Spain's U-19 team at the World Student Games in Mexico City, scoring a penalty in a 10–0 win over Cuba and being injured in a tackle during a 0–0 draw against Canada, which sidelined him for a year. In 1981, he joined Tercera División side Parla on loan, later signing permanently and helping them gain promotion to Segunda División B, and also played three games for Spain Universities XI. In 1985, he signed for Segunda División B club Linares, serving as player/coach under Enrique Mateos, but missed almost the entire 1985–86 season due to injuries and retired as a player. In 1986, at age 26, he returned to Real Madrid to join the coaching staff, becoming coach of Real Madrid Castilla in the 1986–87 season, winning league titles in 1987 and 1989, and a third title with the youth team in 1990. He succeeded José Antonio Camacho as under-19 coach in 1990, winning the Spain Under 19s Cup in 1991 and 1993, defeating Barcelona in both finals, and completing a double in 1993 by winning the national under-19 league. He earned his coaching certificate in 1989 and taught at a football camp at the University of California in Davis in 1990. During the 1992–93 season, he worked as assistant coach to Mariano García Remón at Real Madrid B. After succeeding García Remón in the 1993–94 season, he made his debut as Segunda División manager on 4 September 1993 with a 3–1 win over Hércules. In March 1994, he became assistant to Vicente del Bosque with the senior Real Madrid team and returned to coach Real Madrid B in the 1994–95 season. His first senior management roles outside Real Madrid were unsuccessful: he was dismissed after two wins in 23 games at Real Valladolid in the 1995–96 season and after one win in nine games at Osasuna in the 1996–97 season. He met fitness instructor Pako Ayestarán at Osasuna and formed a partnership with him at several clubs over the next decade. In 1997, he joined Extremadura in the Segunda División and led them to promotion, finishing second behind Alavés after winning 23 out of 42 games. He resigned at Extremadura and took a year off to study in England and Italy, working as a commentator/analyst for Eurosport, Marca, El Mundo, and local Madrid TV. In 2000, he was appointed manager of Tenerife, winning promotion to La Liga by finishing third. In 2001, he was appointed coach of Valencia, replacing Héctor Cúper, who had led the club to two Champions League finals. Valencia had approached Javier Irureta, Mané, and Luis Aragonés, all of whom declined. Club director Javier Subirats advocated for Benítez, and the squad was won over by his modesty, as he stated: "You come from the Champions League final and I come from Segunda División, but humbly I think I have tools to make you improve." He signed a two-year deal with an annual salary of €450,000, below Cúper's €1.2 million. He introduced a more attacking style of play and brought in Mista and Francisco Rufete, with Mista scoring 19 goals in the 2003–04 season. In 2002, Valencia won their first La Liga title in 31 years, finishing seven points ahead of Deportivo La Coruña. The following season, they finished 18 points behind Real Madrid and missed the top four by one point, and Benítez made his Champions League debut, reaching the quarter-finals before losing to Inter Milan. In 2003–04, Valencia won La Liga with three games to spare and beat Marseille 2–0 in the UEFA Cup final. He fell out with Jesús García Pitarch over control of new signings, saying: "I was hoping for a sofa [a defender] and they've brought me a lamp [Fabián Canobbio]," and resigned on 1 June 2004. On 16 June 2004, he was appointed manager of Liverpool, replacing Gérard Houllier. He stated: "It is like a dream to be here. I am very, very proud to be joining one of the most important clubs in the world in one of the best leagues in the world – and I want to win." One of his first tasks was to convince captain Steven Gerrard not to move to Chelsea. He failed to convince Michael Owen to extend his contract, who was sold to Real Madrid. He signed several players from La Liga, including Luis García and Xabi Alonso. In his first season, Liverpool finished fifth in the Premier League due to key player injuries and failed to challenge Chelsea or Arsenal. He reached his first English domestic cup final, losing the League Cup to Chelsea 3–2 after extra time. In the Champions League, Liverpool advanced from the group stages after a 3–1 win over Olympiacos on a 87th-minute goal by Gerrard, progressing to the last 16. After defeating Bayer Leverkusen and Juventus, they reached the semi-final against Chelsea, winning 1–0 on aggregate after a controversial early goal by Luis García. They advanced to the final against Milan, where they came from 3–0 down at half time to level at 3–3 in six minutes, eventually winning 3–2 on penalties with goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek. Benítez became only the third manager in history (after Bob Paisley and José Mourinho) to win the UEFA Cup and Champions League in successive seasons and the second Liverpool manager (after Joe Fagan) to win the Champions League in his first season. Dudek was replaced as first-choice goalkeeper by Pepe Reina starting in the 2005–06 season. Benítez also discarded Vladimír Šmicer and Igor Bišćan, and sold Josemi and Antonio Núñez after they failed to establish themselves, bringing in Peter Crouch, Mohamed Sissoko, Daniel Agger, and Robbie Fowler. His signings improved Liverpool's Premier League form, finishing third, missing second by one point. Liverpool won the FA Cup, defeating Manchester United and Chelsea, and a 5–3 win over Luton Town in the third round, before defeating West Ham United in a dramatic 3–3 draw that led to a penalty shoot-out. Pepe Reina saved three penalties to secure the trophy. After winning the Community Shield 2–1 over Chelsea, the media predicted Liverpool would challenge Chelsea for the 2006–07 title. However, the challenge fizzled out due to poor away form, leading to speculation about Benítez's future, with his agent suggesting a move to Italy. He reaffirmed his desire to remain with Liverpool. Supporters and new owners George Gillett and Tom Hicks welcomed him, with Gillett praising Benítez as a "brilliant coach" and "very sharp, savvy businessman." Benítez demanded transfer market support from the owners, which was not fully provided, and the club showed little activity in the transfer window. He broke Liverpool's transfer record by signing Fernando Torres from Atlético Madrid, along with Ryan Babel, Yossi Benayoun, Lucas Leiva, and Andriy Voronin, and sold Craig Bellamy after an altercation with John Arne Riise. Liverpool topped the Premier League table in the 2007–08 season after a 6–0 win over Derby County. Despite this, poor Champions League results and a disagreement over future transfers led to a public falling-out with the owners, which was covered in the media. A fans' march in support of Benítez occurred ahead of a 4–1 win over Porto. It was later revealed that Jürgen Klinsmann had been offered Benítez's job before accepting the Bayern Munich role, damaging relations with Americans and fueling rumors of a return to Real Madrid. Benítez stated his future was at Liverpool and appointed Sammy Lee as his new assistant to replace Pako Ayestarán. Despite the lack of trophies, the main issues were off the pitch, with a power struggle between Benítez and the Liverpool board. In the summer of 2008, Benítez was reportedly close to quitting over the board's failure to support his bid to purchase Gareth Barry from Aston Villa.

It was later revealed that Jürgen Klinsmann had been offered Benítez's job at Liverpool before eventually accepting the position of Bayern Munich manager, which damaged Benítez's relationship with American media, as constant rumors linked him with a return to Real Madrid. Benítez affirmed that his future remained with Liverpool and appointed Sammy Lee as his new assistant to replace Pako Ayestarán, who resigned after a reported disagreement. During Liverpool's domestic campaign, Benítez failed to win any trophies, including a shock FA Cup exit at home to Barnsley and a loss to Chelsea in the Champions League semi-finals. The main issues were off the pitch, with Benítez involved in a power struggle with the Liverpool board. In the summer of 2008, Benítez reportedly considered quitting over the board's refusal to support his bid to buy Gareth Barry from Aston Villa, intending to sell Xabi Alonso to fund the purchase, but Liverpool CEO Rick Parry prioritized signing Robbie Keane instead, leading to Barry not joining. Keane was later re-sold to Tottenham Hotspur in January, with some analysts calling him a "pawn in a power struggle" between Benítez and the club's owners. Despite this, Liverpool started the 2008–09 season strongly, including Benítez's first league win against Manchester United at Anfield on 13 September and ending Chelsea's 86-match unbeaten league run at Stamford Bridge. Liverpool finished the year top of the Premier League for the first time since 1996. However, poor results in the New Year intensified scrutiny, especially after Benítez missed a December draw against Arsenal due to kidney stone surgery. An infamous media attack on Manchester United manager Sir Alex Ferguson led some pundits and opposition fans to suggest Benítez was "cracking up" under pressure. He publicly rejected a contract extension and demanded greater control over transfers, with rumors of his departure becoming so widespread that bookmakers suspended betting on the issue. On 18 March 2009, shortly after victories over Real Madrid and Manchester United, Benítez signed a five-year deal, stating, "My heart is with Liverpool, so I'm delighted to sign this new deal, I love the club, the fans and the city and with a club and supporters like this, I could never say no to staying." With ten wins in their last 11 games, Liverpool finished second in the league for the first time under Benítez, four points behind champions Manchester United, playing an attractive attacking style in contrast to their winter struggles. Before his final season, Xabi Alonso was sold to Real Madrid in a £30 million deal, with Alonso stating Benítez's attempts to sell him were a deciding factor. Alonso was replaced by Italian midfielder Alberto Aquilani, signed from Roma for £17 million, who was recovering from injury, and England defender Glen Johnson, signed for £17.5 million. A "sell to buy" policy enforced by ownership due to rising debt, combined with Alonso's departure, caused discontent among fans who believed Benítez was not supported in transfers. Benítez defended his decisions, claiming Liverpool's slow start was due to key players like Steven Gerrard being below par. Liverpool's worst run in 22 years, combined with a Champions League group stage exit, led to the first major fan criticism, with some suggesting the team lacked Benítez's defensive rigidity despite conceding fewer goals than Manchester United and Chelsea and lacking depth when key players like Gerrard and Fernando Torres were injured. The club also exited the UEFA Europa League to Atlético Madrid. Benítez left the club "by mutual consent" on 3 June 2010 with a reported £6 million pay-off; media speculated this was due to finishing seventh in the Premier League, missing Champions League qualification, and poor results including a defeat by Wigan Athletic. Shortly after leaving, Benítez made a £96,000 donation to the Hillsborough Family Support Group. On 10 June 2010, just days after leaving Liverpool, he agreed to become head coach of Serie A champions Inter Milan, taking over from José Mourinho, who left to manage Real Madrid. On 15 June 2010, he was presented to Italian media after signing a two-year deal. On 21 August 2010, he won his first trophy, the Italian Super Cup, defeating Roma 3–1. On 27 August 2010, Inter lost to Atlético Madrid in the 2010 UEFA Super Cup. His first Serie A match was a 0–0 draw away to Bologna on 31 August 2010. His first league win came on 11 September 2010, a 2–1 victory over Udinese at San Siro. By December 2010, Inter had dropped to sixth in Serie A, 13 points behind the top (with two games in hand), after consecutive defeats to Milan (ending a 46-match unbeaten home record), Chievo, Lazio, and a loss at Tottenham in the Champions League, leading to speculation about his position. Despite criticism, Benítez led Inter to win the FIFA Club World Cup in December 2010. After the victory, he urged the club to back him with new signings or consider replacing him, but ownership, led by Massimo Moratti, dismissed his demands. On 23 December 2010, just five days after the Club World Cup win, Benítez was dismissed. On 21 November 2012, following Roberto Di Matteo's dismissal, Chelsea appointed Benítez as interim manager until the end of the 2012–13 season. He was officially unveiled as manager on 22 November 2012 and appointed Boudewijn Zenden as assistant. The appointment was unpopular due to Benítez's past association with Liverpool and previous comments about Chelsea, resulting in a "fiercely hostile reception" at his first home game, a 0–0 draw with Manchester City on 25 November 2012, followed by a 0–0 draw against Fulham and a 3–1 loss to West Ham. On 5 December 2012, he recorded his first win, a 6–1 victory over Nordsjælland in the Champions League, though Chelsea failed to progress beyond the group stage. His first league win came on a 3–1 away victory over Sunderland. At the 2012 FIFA Club World Cup, Chelsea defeated Monterrey 3–1 to reach the final, losing 1–0 to Corinthians. They advanced to the League Cup semi-finals with a 5–1 win over Leeds United and an 8–0 victory over Aston Villa, equalling their record top-flight win. They were then eliminated by Swansea City 2–0 on aggregate in the semi-finals. On 27 February 2013, after a 2–0 win at Middlesbrough in the FA Cup fifth round, Benítez criticized the board for calling him "interim" and the fans for their protests, confirming he would leave at the end of the season. He described his relationship with owner Roman Abramovich as "excellent" and expressed a desire to stay until the end of the season. Results remained mixed, with Chelsea 16 points behind leaders Manchester United when he took over. Chelsea reached the FA Cup semi-finals, losing 2–1 to Manchester City at Wembley, and advanced to the UEFA Europa League final. In the penultimate league game, Chelsea won 2–1 away to Aston Villa, with Frank Lampard setting the all-time scoring record. The win secured a top-four finish and a Champions League spot in the next season. In the Europa League final on 15 May, Chelsea won 2–1, making Benítez only the second manager after Giovanni Trapattoni to win the UEFA Cup/Europa League with two different teams, and Chelsea became the fourth club overall and the first in Britain to win all three major European trophies. Defender David Luiz credited Benítez with making tactical changes at half time, saying, "He changed some of our positions in the second half. That's why we played better and won the title. He spoke a lot to us to change the intensity." On the winning goal by Branislav Ivanović, Juan Mata said, "Rafa told us we had to aim for the far post, because it was Artur's weakest place. I just tried to put the ball there and Ivanović did the rest." On 19 May, in his final competitive match, Benítez led Chelsea to a 2–1 home win over Everton, securing third place in the Premier League and a direct spot in the following season's Champions League group stage. Benítez did not participate in the lap of honour, but many fans showed appreciation, contrasting with the initial hostility. On 27 May 2013, it was announced Benítez signed for Napoli, following Walter Mazzarri's resignation. He agreed to a two-year contract after meeting club president Aurelio De Laurentiis in London. In his first season, Benítez led Napoli to victory in the Coppa Italia, defeating Fiorentina 3–1 in the final, and reached the last 16 of the Europa League, exiting after a 3–2 aggregate loss to Porto. Napoli finished third in Serie A in 2013–14, qualifying for the next season's Champions League. They lost 4–2 on aggregate to Athletic Bilbao in the qualifying stages and entered the Europa League. Benítez announced he would resign at the end of the 2014–15 season. His final match was a 4–2 defeat to Lazio, who secured the final Champions League spot. On 3 June 2015, Benítez was confirmed as Real Madrid manager, signing a three-year contract. Real Madrid remained unbeaten in the league until a 3–2 loss at Sevilla on the eleventh matchday, followed by a 4–0 home loss to Barcelona in the first Clásico. Madrid won away 3–1 against Cádiz in the Copa del Rey round of 32, but was disqualified in the second leg for fielding an ineligible player. Meanwhile, Real topped their Champions League group with 16 points. On 4 January 2016, Benítez's contract was terminated due to allegations of unpopularity with supporters, player displeasure, and poor results against top teams. At the time of dismissal, Real were third in La Liga, four points behind leaders Atlético Madrid and two points behind Barcelona, who had a game in hand. On 11 March 2016, Benítez was appointed manager of relegation-threatened Newcastle United, signing a three-year deal. He lost his first match, 1–0 away to eventual champions Leicester City on 14 March. He won his first game in his fifth match, 3–0 over Swansea City on 16 April. Newcastle ended the season with a six-match unbeaten run, including a 5–1 final-day win over third-place Tottenham Hotspur. However, the team was relegated due to rivals Sunderland claiming 12 points from their final six fixtures. On 25 May 2016, it was confirmed Benítez would remain as manager. In May 2017, Newcastle achieved promotion and returned to the Premier League after one season in the Championship. On 24 June 2019, Newcastle announced Benítez would step down upon contract expiration. Mike Ashley criticized him, stating his demands made it impossible to remain in charge. In a December 2020 interview with The Athletic, Benítez said he had no choice but to leave due to disagreements with Ashley, describing him as "a businessman who I don't believe really cares about his team." Two of Benítez's signings, Fabian Schär and Jacob Murphy, went on to play in the 2025 EFL Cup final and became part of the first Newcastle United team to win a major trophy in 70 years. On 2 July 2019, Benítez was appointed manager of Chinese Super League side Dalian Professional (formerly Dalian Yifang), signing a two-and-a-half-year deal. On 23 January 2021, he left the club by mutual consent, citing concerns over family health due to the COVID-19 pandemic. On 30 June 2021, Benítez was appointed manager of Premier League club Everton on a three-year contract, replacing Carlo Ancelotti, who left to rejoin Real Madrid. Before signing, he faced threats from a group of Everton supporters who left a banner near his home reading: "We know where you live. Don't sign." Benítez is only the second person to manage both Liverpool and Everton since William Edward Barclay in the 1890s. Under Benítez, Everton began with a winning streak in their first four games, including a 3–1 win over Southampton, which was followed by a 2–2 draw at Leeds United, a 2–1 EFL Cup win over Huddersfield Town, and a 2–0 Premier League win against Brighton & Hove Albion. The unbeaten run earned him a Manager of the Month nomination. However, form declined in the following months, with the club winning only one game (2–1 against Arsenal) between matchdays 7 and 22. After a 2–1 defeat to bottom-placed Norwich City at Carrow Road, Benítez was relieved of his duties on 16 January 2022, after six-and-a-half months in charge, with Everton in 15th place, six points above the relegation zone.

Rafael Benítez is only the second person to manage both Liverpool and Everton, following William Edward Barclay in the 1890s. Under his management, Everton began with a winning streak in the Premier League and EFL Cup, winning their first league game 3–1 against Southampton, followed by a 2–2 draw at Leeds United, a 2–1 victory over Huddersfield Town in the EFL Cup, and a 2–0 win against Brighton & Hove Albion in the Premier League, leading to his nomination for Manager of the Month. However, Everton's form declined, with only one win—against Arsenal—between matchdays 7 and 22, and after a 2–1 loss to Norwich City, Benítez was dismissed on 16 January 2022 after six-and-a-half months in charge, with the club in 15th place, six points above the relegation zone, having lost nine of their previous thirteen games; he became the fifth Everton manager to be sacked in the previous six years. On 23 June 2023, he was appointed manager of La Liga club Celta Vigo on a three-year contract, replacing Carlos Carvalhal. On 12 March 2024, he was sacked after accumulating just five wins and 24 points from 28 matches, leaving the club two points from relegation; he had led Celta to the quarterfinals of the Copa del Rey for the first time since 2017, losing 1–2 to Real Sociedad in January, and his final match in charge ended in a 4–0 defeat to Real Madrid. On 19 October 2025, Benítez became manager of Panathinaikos on a 2.5-year contract. He has had public confrontations with José Mourinho (Chelsea manager from 2004 to 2007) and Sir Alex Ferguson of Manchester United, suggesting Mourinho's success was due to Roman Abramovich's money and refusing to shake hands after some matches, though Mourinho claimed the feud ended in 2006; when Mourinho left in 2007, Benítez declined to comment, as did Ferguson and Arsène Wenger. On 9 January 2009, Benítez criticized Ferguson, accusing him and Manchester United of being nervous due to Liverpool's top league position and claiming Ferguson was not punished for FA rule-breaking after comments about officials, stating he was "the only manager in the league that cannot be punished for these things"; in his 2013 autobiography, Ferguson said Benítez "bought badly and made the feud personal." Benítez also had clashes with Sam Allardyce during his time at Newcastle United and Blackburn Rovers; Allardyce claimed Benítez would have been dismissed if Liverpool's European form had been as poor as their league form, and in April 2009 accused Benítez of arrogance after a gesture during a Blackburn match, suggesting he signaled the game was over despite a two-goal lead, a view later supported by Ferguson; Benítez clarified that the gesture was a joke to instruct Xabi Alonso to ignore a free-kick instruction, not to indicate the game was over. Benítez developed a reputation as a difficult manager to please, with former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard expressing a longing for a "well done" after strong performances; he also removed most of his Champions League-winning squad members within four seasons, with penalty shoot-out hero Jerzy Dudek relegated to backup goalkeeper the season after the European triumph. His preferred formation is 4–2–3–1, adopted during his time at Valencia and Liverpool; he is highly regarded for his tactical acumen, especially in European competitions, where he set up teams to exploit opposition weaknesses. In the 2005 UEFA Champions League final, his calmness and tactical adjustments at half-time gave players confidence to fight back from 3–0 down, though he had to adjust his plan when it was noted his formation required 12 players on the pitch. He frequently played key players in unorthodox positions, notably converting Steven Gerrard and Dirk Kuyt into right-wingers; as a right winger/midfielder, Gerrard had his most productive seasons in trophies, winning a Champions League and an FA Cup. Benítez believes in squad rotation and zonal marking, despite heavy criticism from the English press; he achieved Champions League and FA Cup victories in his first two seasons through rotation to keep key players fit. Zonal marking was criticized when Liverpool conceded from set-pieces, though Benítez's teams are known for strong defense and low goals conceded; he defended the tactic, noting that teams using man-marking concede just as many, if not more, from set pieces. At the end of the 2008–09 season, Benítez introduced backroom changes to improve youth development, including appointing club legend Kenny Dalglish to a senior role at the academy. Benítez's father, Francisco, worked as a hotelier; his mother is Rosario Maudes, a Real Madrid fan, while his father supported Atlético Madrid; Francisco died in December 2005 while Benítez was in Japan for the FIFA Club World Championship. Benítez married Maria Montserrat in 1998; they have two daughters, born in Madrid in 1999 and in Valencia in 2002. He is fluent in Spanish, English, French, and Italian.
